title: Seller ops briefing: latency & risk mitigations (sketch)
body:
Purpose:
A compact seller-facing briefing + ops checklist to handle customer questions about latency, availability, and fallback economics during pilot conversations. Focused on quick, defensible guidance sellers can use live with engineers and platform architects (30–60s soundbites + checklist for request to ops).

Status: WIP — share with SEs for feedback. This is intentionally sketchy: want short cards, clear mitigations, and a minimal runbook for pilots.

Top-line elevator for customers (30s):
- Redwood focuses on predictable, production-grade inference. If a route experiences high latency or capacity pressure we can: (1) fall back to a compatible model variant in the same region, (2) route to reserved capacity / Dedicated pools for consistent p95, or (3) enable prefix/KV caching for repeated queries to cut tail latency and cost.
- We trade gracefully: small quality delta for big improvements in latency/cost when needed.

Common customer objections and 1-line seller responses:
- "LLM latency is too variable for our UI": "We give you routing policies and can pin model variants to Dedicated capacity; if you need sub-200ms targets we’ll map your endpoint to reserved pools and prewarm caches as part of pilot."
- "We can’t sacrifice quality for speed": "We run short A/B on canary traffic—if the fallback model shows >1–2% metric drift we revert automatically; we also keep full audit logs so you can measure production regressions."
- "What if my traffic spikes?": "Autoscaling + burst policies on Dedicated plus auto-fallback to hosted variants keeps the app responsive while we bring capacity online."

Technical signal cards (for quick SE use)
- Fallback routing (fast wins):
  - Policy: If p95 >SLO for N seconds, route X% of new requests to fallback model Y (lower cost or quantized).
  - When to use: short capacity events, cost mitigation, or temporary regional outages.
  - Typical trade: 3–8% quality drop vs 30–60% latency reduction (depends on model family).

- Prefix/KV caching (app-level optimization):
  - Use when interactions have shared context or repeated prompts (e.g., chat with repeated system prompt).
  - Expected impact: 20–60% token cost reduction, significant p95 improvement on repeated flows.
  - Note: requires minor SDK config changes (cache TTL, cache key composition).

- Dedicated pools + model pinning:
  - Use for strict p95/p99 SLOs and regulatory isolation.
  - Sellers script: "We can reserve X GPUs for your critical endpoints and guarantee throughput Y for token lengths up to Z."

Metrics cheat-sheet (rapid quoting)
- Sample targets (for conversation):
  - Interactive chat (short context): p50 30–80ms, p95 120–220ms (hosted) — Dedicated can target p95 <120ms depending on model/GPUs.
  - Long-context generation (2k tokens): p50 200–400ms per token, p95 varies widely.
- Cost delta shorthand: Dedicated reservation reduces per-token cost by ~20–40% at scale vs best-effort hosted (very workload dependant).

Pilot kickstart checklist (ops-ready, 1–2 page handoff)
- Before pilot: collect
  - Example prompts + representative workload (percent distribution by prompt length)
  - Expected qps and traffic shape (burstiness, daily patterns)
  - SLO target: p50/p95 and acceptable quality delta (if fallback used)
  - Compliance or data residency needs

- Quick config items to set in pilot:
  - Routing policy: primary model + fallback matrix (model id + percent split)
  - Cache config: enable prefix cache? TTLs? key schema?
  - Autoscale: min/max workers on Dedicated; burst pool enabled?
  - Observability: add route-level tracing and token-level cost reporting to dashboard

- Go/no-go triggers (promote to Dedicated / escalate to solutions):
  - Sustained p95 breach > 10% of calls for 15 minutes
  - Quality regression on canary > agreed tolerance
  - Cost per 1k tokens > threshold 

Live objection scripts (copyable):
- Customer: "We need consistent 99th percentile latency."
  - Seller: "Understood. For pilots we map the route to a Dedicated pool, enable prewarming and prefix caching; that typically eliminates cold tails and gives you an SLO-backed p99 target. If you want, we can instrument custom traces so your SREs can validate in real time."

- Customer: "I’m worried about fallback accuracy."
  - Seller: "We always run a canary set—fallbacks are introduced gradually and monitored against your eval prompts. If the delta exceeds your threshold we automatically rollback and notify your team."

Example short play (scripted):
1) Discovery: capture top-10 prompts & traffic shape.
2) Quick bench: run these on hosted primary + 1 fallback; capture latency/cost/qa metrics. (link to bench doc: confluence:bench-GT-2025)
3) Recommend config: routing policy, cache TTL, Dedicated sizing estimate.
4) Roll pilot for 48–72 hours. Monitor p95 and evals.

Ops troubleshooting cheats (for SEs and SREs)
- If p95 spikes but p50 is stable: look for tail-causing requests (longer prompts or rare tokens) – try max tokens limit or dynamic batching threshold adjustments.
- If latency spikes and CPU/GPU usage low: investigate network region mismatch or routing misconfiguration.
- If quality drops after enabling quantized fallback: revert fallback and run a lighter quantization profile; capture diff on eval set.

Unresolved / TODO (needs SE input):
- Produce 3 short listening cards (30s) for AE playbook: one for midmarket, one for platform architects, one for enterprise procurement.
- One-pager with exact example numbers (p50/p95 and cost delta) for top 5 open models — need input from Applied ML benchmarking team.
- Add quick demo script for post-demo follow-up email with suggested config snippet.

Links and refs (internal):
- latency playbook (confluence:INF-ops-latency-playbook)
- canonical bench scripts (github:repo/benchmarks/tree/main/chat)
- pilot handoff ticket template (JIRA:GT-1234)

Notes to self:
- Keep phrasing non-committal in public decks: "can target" vs "guarantee" until we have legal signoff for SLA language.
- This doc should map to a 1-slide cheat card + 1 page ops checklist variant for SEs.

End of sketch.

If this looks useful I’ll iterate into two artifacts: (1) a single-slide cheat card for seller decks, (2) a 1-page ops-handoff template for pilot engineers. Feedback wanted: which three quick numbers should we default to when quoting p95 for pilot sizing?
